messages:
marie: Heads-up — I tracked down a small repro where the Go SDK double-submits a request after a 429 + token refresh. Put together a minimal sample app and logs: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-go-429-double-replay (repro steps in the gist).

kai: Thanks — is this only happening for the sync endpoints or streaming too?

marie: Repro is sync, but we also observed a similar resume+retry pattern in streaming when the client reconnects after auth refresh. The sync repro is simplest to iterate on.

sasha: Quick question: are the Go and Python SDKs using the same jitter approach? I thought python uses full jitter by default.

ben: Go client currently uses equal_jitter (from our retries package). Python uses full_jitter. Also, our auth refresh flow does: request -> 401/429 -> refresh token -> replay original request. If we don't set an idempotency header, the server treats the replay as a new request.

marie: Adding an Idempotency-Key header locally fixes the double-processing in the repro. But SDKs should offer a safer default: consistent jitter across SDKs + optional auto idempotency for non-streaming requests.

kai: Sounds reasonable. Proposed actions: (1) change Go default jitter to full_jitter to match python, (2) add an opt-in config to enable auto-generated Idempotency-Key for non-streaming requests (opt-out), (3) update sample apps and docs. Any concerns?

sasha: I like it, but caution: auto idempotency could hide app-level semantics. Make it opt-in by default? Or opt-out? For backwards compatibility I'd prefer opt-in, but we can ship a beta with opt-in + telemetry. Also we should ensure keys TTL limited (server-side) and make users aware.

ben: Implementation idea: RetryOptions struct with fields -> EnableAutoIdempotency (bool), AutoIdempotencyTTLSeconds (int), JitterStrategy (string). Default in beta: EnableAutoIdempotency=false, but we provide a quick sample toggle and a compatibility guide. I'll draft the patch.

marie: Sample app patch (Go) — helper I used in the repro: 

```go
func genIdempotencyKey() string {
    return fmt.Sprintf("sdk-go-%d-%s", time.Now().UnixNano(), uuid.New().String())
}
req.Header.Set("Idempotency-Key", genIdempotencyKey())
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```

With that + full_jitter I ran a 1k request run and observed zero duplicate processing. Logs attached in gist.

deploy-bot: deploy:devex-sampleapp 1763012347 - sampleapp:deploy succeeded :white_check_mark:

sasha: We should also emit telemetry when the SDK auto-generates idempotency keys so we can measure how often it triggers and any downstream unexpected outcomes (tag with sdk.language and endpoint).

ben: Agreed. I'll add metric "sdk.auto_idempotency_used" with tags: {lang: "go", opt_in: true/false}.

kai: :thumbsup: Please open two PRs: one against eng-runtime for the jitter/retry behavior and telemetry, and one against devex/sampleapps + docs for the sample and guidance. Assign to eng-runtime and devex for review.

marie: I'll open the PRs today. Preliminary results in the PR: 1000 reqs, mean latency unchanged, duplicates dropped to 0 with idempotency + full_jitter. Will include benchmarks.

ben: I'll review the runtime PR. If no blockers by EOD we'll promote to beta.

sasha: Nice find and solid repro — thanks for digging in marie :raised_hands:

marie: Thanks all. I'll link the PRs here when ready.
